concepts.title: Psychology as the Science of Mind and Behaviour

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Psychology as the Science of Mind and Behaviour' refers to.
questions.a: Psychology is the scientific study of mental processes and behaviour: how we think, feel, perceive, remember and act. Its scientific character lies in method -- systematic observation and measurement -- rather than in white coats, and its subject matter includes both inner experience and outward action.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Psychology as the Science of Mind and Behaviour'.
questions.a: A science of the inner and the outer -- mental processes and behaviour studied by systematic method.

concepts.title: Growth of the Discipline: From Philosophy to Modern Psychology

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Growth of the Discipline: From Philosophy to Modern Psychology' refers to.
questions.a: Psychology's questions are ancient but its science is young: born from philosophy and physiology, it grew through schools such as structuralism, functionalism, behaviourism, Gestalt and psychoanalysis into today's cognitive and humanistic approaches, each adding a window on the person.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Growth of the Discipline: From Philosophy to Modern Psychology'.
questions.a: Old questions, young science -- each historical school added one more window on the mind.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Growth of the Discipline: From Philosophy to Modern Psychology' taught, and from which source text?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Fields and Applications of Psychology' refers to.
questions.a: Psychology branches into fields of study and work: cognitive, developmental and social psychology, and applied streams -- clinical and counselling psychology, organisational and educational psychology, sports and health psychology -- each applying the science to human problems in its arena.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Fields and Applications of Psychology'.
questions.a: One science, many arenas -- from clinic to classroom to playground, psychology applies wherever people act.
